insight.title: Why the humble shipping container runs the world
insight.subtitle: A simple metal box made global trade possible and cheap.

sections.text: Long ago, moving goods was slow and very expensive. Workers carried individual sacks and barrels onto wooden ships by hand. This process took days or even weeks to complete. Because loading was so difficult, items from far away cost a fortune. Most people only bought things made in their local town.

In the 1950s, a businessman had a brilliant idea to use standard metal boxes. These containers could fit perfectly on trucks, trains, and massive ships. Suddenly, moving goods became a seamless puzzle. Instead of handling every item, machines moved the boxes quickly. This efficiency dropped the cost of shipping to almost nothing.

Today, these metal boxes allow companies to build products across many different countries. Your phone and clothes likely traveled halfway around the globe inside one. This system connects every nation into a single giant marketplace. It is the reason why almost any product you want is affordable and easily available today.

news.title: Britain blocking use of air bases Trump says would be needed for strikes on Iran, UK media report
news.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has reportedly blocked a request from US President Donald Trump to allow US forces to use UK air bases during any preemptive attack on Iran, owing to concerns it would be in breach of international law, according to multiple reports in British media citing government sources.
